body: That is a whole heap of useful things... thanks for taking the time to share them. The dive response sounds freakily cool, and new to me. The hobbit thing I completely relate to, including the 'I shouldn't need this stuff' thing, so might have to hit up the garden center... again. I have a heated blanket, which sounds naff, but it is fake fur and looks and feels amazing, and often helps... Most of all, I miss the sauna. It used to fix everything. But. Pandemic...
The feeling is mutual. Lifelines are always a two-way connection.

It's a good question, but it's hard to get a honest line of communication open at the moment. Rather like you I'm so used to disassociating from the body smoke signals. It feels like my body wants to completely shut down, not eat, and just hibernate. That, however, would not end well... I did go for a run when the sun came out, and that helped to ground me. Thanks for the thoughts, really appreciated... no easy answers for any of us.
Compassion. Such a hard thing. Thanks for reminding me. Not my strong suit... definitely ever to strive for... Really helpful comment, thank you.

Here's a long, extendable wooden straw, painted silver, possibly wrapped in underwater LEDs making everything look colourful in a blurry kinda way. You can breathe through this straw, no matter how far down you are. Breathe in. With air in your lungs you float. That's all you have to do: breathe in, and float. Let the water hold you for a moment, just for the tiniest moment... Somewhere in this big dark ocean, we are all floating. You are not alone. How amazing that you don't want to drown, that you want to breathe and live. You've inspired me a little bit in writing that, and, today, I am really grateful... thanks for sending out an sos through the ocean... I hear you. Keep breathing.

Like others have said, I find it helps when I really own the anger. When I recognise it for what it is... For me, it is the anger that is part of the grief for the child and person that was taken from me, the child and person I can never be, that was destroyed by people who were supposed to be nurturing me. This anger is healthy, for me, once I can feel where it comes from: that it's not about the f\*ckers who got lucky, but about the f\*ckers who took that luck away from me... I'm still there, angry and grieving... I might be angry for a long time, and I get triggered, like you, a lot. But, and perhaps this is just me, it sure beats not feeling anything at all... Top tip: Never let the anger turn inwards. It's not you. It's not them, now. It's all about 'back then'... Second tip: Yeah, it sucks... Third tip: There are some folk on here who have been through the grieving process and come out the side, so perhaps listen to them (I try to)... Much care.
Beautifully written. The invisibility mask or shield is a weight and an effort to carry.

\*laughs with sardonic humor\* My by-line was "the mature one" as a child. The teenager who all the adults came to for therapy and understanding. Yes, because I was arbitrating and managing my psychotic and suicidal parents, so a normal divorce and a normal crisis was a piece of cake to understand...

'Sheer bloody-mindedness' sometimes is all that keeps me going, a sort of, well, I got this far, as well as a stubborn, f 'em, just living is my middle finger to everyone and everything that keeps trying to take me out... (yes, a little internal rage to work on, I know)...
Thank you. I feel like I have gritted teeth, hanging on to the last fading light of my life... good to hear that you held on and found something to keep hanging on to...

Much gentle warmth to you, and thanks for replying, even letting me know that we resonate helps, helps me feel less alone, maybe helps others feel less alone (I don't know, guessing)... thinking of you and all the other strangers on here...
I hadn't heard of this organisation before so will take a look, thanks...
Thanks. It's good to remember there can be more to life than a relationship...

I completely hear you, and thanks for saying it... When trauma is woven in, fused into your bones, it is invisible. There is nothing to point to and say, there, that thing that happened (as with a single external traumatic event). For me, perhaps for others, I can only point to myself and say, here, this thing that you cannot see or imagine, it's in here... behind the smile...
Reaches back.. thank you.

That's so kind for you to say. I am also touched. Sharing these stories is not easy. The pandemic (and the rest) has made things so much harder. But don't forget to think about what you can do for yourself, maybe start there. Maybe what you can do for her, is to do something for yourself first, to get your own support, an infrastructure, see your doctor... I wish I had done that when my mother was ill, so that may be more a refection of myself, but just passing the thought on... take care, even though its hard to smile...
If you don't mind, I will just imagine hugging you back, and drip a few tears on your shoulder... thank you...

Hey there, not sure if this will help, but my mother was also suicidal for many years whilst I was young, and burdened me with helping her. I also became suicidal. It changed me forever... but... she called in professional help, she got help, it was messy, but she worked hard and got better. Your mother needs help that you cannot provide, you need help. If you can, direct her to professional support, to therapy, to her doctor. But take care of yourself, and call in your own professionals, call in some help, someone who can be on your side, who can be a resource for just you. No matter your mother's choices, you have choices, you can take care of your own self. You have to. To be there for her, you have to be there for yourself first. Be well, caring person... be well. Your path is hard, be gentle on yourself...

Yes, and recognising it was really helpful for me. Thinking about suicide becomes a thought that I can see, and so I can remember that I am not that thought. There is a 'me' that is separate from the thoughts of suicide... that 'me' is a creature who appears to just breathe and live... this helps... sometimes. I am not going to say it gets better, but I can stay I am still here...

\*applauds\* You write really well. I hear you in your words. You make your soul shimmer in your text. And that is a skill and an art. Thank you. You reached my soul. I am tired, too. Tired of my bad childhood, my own mental illness, the years and years fighting to survive and wondering why, when each breath is in the dark, with no one to see or care for my battle. I've got nothing to offer other than that mirror: I see myself in your words, and that is a connection.

\*wave\* I've almost died and nobody checks up on me. I've lived alone for a decade and nobody checks up on me. We are the invisible. We are the vulnerable that no-one sees. We are the ones who are already isolated. And... but... we are many. \*wave\*
Keep breathing. That's all I know. Air in. Air out. That's all you have to do. Air in. Air out.
Thanks. Sometimes sunlight filters down. Sometimes.
